coordinate_and_scale_contract.world_unit_scale: 1 Three.js world unit = 1 modular grid tile (1.0m nominal)
coordinate_and_scale_contract.room_origin_convention: South-West (SW) floor corner at [0, 0, 0]; room extends across X=[0..8] (West->East) and Z=[0..8] (South->North).
coordinate_and_scale_contract.default_front_facing_note: North (+Z) and West (X=0) walls are full height (3.20u); East (X=8) and South (Z=0) are cutaway walls (0.38u) for three-quarter isometric viewing from the South-East quadrant.

runtime_viewer_dependencies: glTF 2.0 does not serialize Three.js Material.polygonOffset parameters; host runtime should re-apply polygonOffset (-1, -2) to Floor_Center_Woven_Rug and Contact_Shadow_* meshes or preserve their physical Y elevation offset (already separated at Y >= 0.004..0.025).
Set magFilter and minFilter to THREE.NearestFilter on imported textures to preserve crisp pixel-art texel edges.
Directional key light shadow bias (-0.0008) and normalBias (0.035) with orthographic near=0.5 / far=48 prevent shadow acne on thin voxel trims.

animation_inventory.note: pm_room.glb is a static architectural and furniture module (0 embedded clips). Character animations belong to boss_pm.glb and BossPMCharacterSystem.ts.

known_limitations: Scene lights, OrbitControls, orthographic camera, and RoomEnvironment IBL are runtime viewer components and are intentionally excluded from pm_room.glb.

Three.js polygonOffset material properties are runtime renderer state and not part of the glTF 2.0 specification; however, all floor rugs, mats, and decals are also physically separated in Y elevation so they do not Z-fight in standard glTF viewers.
